thread_title: Build & quality problems in my brand-new VinFast VF7
post_content: My Two-Month-Old VinFast VF7 Is Falling Apart  And the Company Won't Honour the Warranty By Devinder, a Senior Executive Engineer (Electrical) with a Punjab state power utility Owner, VinFast VF7 (Infinity) · Purchased May 2026, Chandigarh I did not buy a VinFast to write about it. I bought it because I believed in it. After years of spending my professional life around electrical systems, I am a Senior Executive Engineer with one of India's largest state power utilities, I was genuinely excited that a serious global EV maker had come to India. I put a large part of my savings into a VF7 Infinity, drove it home from the Chandigarh showroom in May 2026, and told anyone who would listen that this was the future. Two months later, my car is quite literally coming apart, and the company that sold it to me is refusing to stand behind it. This is what happened, told plainly, with the same eye for cause and effect that my job demands. Month one: a crack appears near the AC vent The first sign of trouble came within roughly a month of delivery. A crack appeared on the dashboard, right beside the air-conditioning vent. There was no impact. Nothing was dropped on it. Nobody sat on it. It simply cracked. As an engineer, I know what thermal stress does to polymers. Automotive grade dashboard plastics are specified precisely so they can survive this for years. A vent surround that fractures in weeks, with no external force, points to inferior grade material. When I raised it at the showroom, the answer was that its not covered under warranty. Around day 45: the taillight fills with water, and a safety system dies The second failure was worse. In July, about 45 days after purchase, the seal on the rear LED taillight opened on its own. The lamp is supposed to be a sealed unit. Water vapour began entering the housing and the LED stopped working. Here is the part that should worry every VF7 owner. To my surprise in this car the systems are interconnected, and when the taillight failed, the Adaptive Cruise Control went inoperative with it. A feature I paid a premium for and a genuine safety system was knocked out by a leaking tail lamp. Moisture inside a sealed lamp, with no collision and no external damage, means the seal or the assembly failed and that this is a manufacturing defect, full stop. I approached the dealership, and then I waited. Fifteen days passed with no meaningful response. Let me be precise about why both of my problems fall squarely inside that line: -The AC-vent crack appeared with no external cause, far too early for a properly specified dashboard polymer. That is a material or moulding defect. -The taillight water ingress occurred with no collision or external damage. Moisture in a sealed lamp can only mean a failed seal  a manufacturing defect. -The Adaptive Cruise Control failure is a consequential fault flowing directly from the defective taillight, not a separate coincidence. None of this is caused by how I drive or park. It is caused by inferior quality materials used on the car and the inability of the aftersales network to fix it. My advice, learned the hard way: photograph every defect the day it appears, keep every invoice and service interaction in writing, and get the dealer's warranty refusal on paper rather than as a verbal not covered. I have preserved all of mine. I am asking VinFast to do the following now through proper written channels: -Give me a written explanation for the warranty denial on the dashboard crack. -Replace the defective rear LED taillight assembly under warranty. -Restore all affected systems, including the Adaptive Cruise Control. -Respond in writing, with a timeline  the silence has been as damaging as the defects. A closing note I still want to be proven right about VinFast. I championed this brand to my colleagues and my community, and I would happily update this post to say the company stepped up and fixed a genuine problem. But a manufacturer's real character shows not when the car is perfect on delivery day, but when something fails and a customer needs it to keep its word. Right now, on both counts, VinFast has let me down. If you are a VF7 owner seeing similar issues: cracked trim, taillight moisture, safety features dropping out, I would genuinely like to hear from you. The more of us who document this clearly, the harder it becomes to wave away.

post_content: ACC or ADAS or ESP(Hill Hold/Brake Hold all comes under it) can automatically apply the brakes based on the specific conditions by design. Subsequently it activates the brake lights via CAN/Brake Light Relay. If the system is capable of sensing a malfunctioning tail light, it will proactively deactivate these systems as a failsafe measure. This is a very good architecture. That being said, If a manufacturer cannot prove a physical impact or tampering, they should honor warranty. EVs are taxed at 5% to encourage early adoption and to help manufacturers. That leaves a very good margin for the manufacturers to support early failures. External damage shouldn't be covered, but legitimate warranty claims shouldn't be rejected without a clear proof of misuse or impact.

post_content: Quote: Originally Posted by loverpool005 My Two-Month-Old VinFast VF7 Is Falling Apart Attachment 2905504 From the photos, the crack in the AC vent does not appear to be a typical thermal failure. The visible scratch adjacent to the crack is more indicative of a prying tool having slipped during an attempt to open the vent. That points towards some form of mechanical interventionpossibly during the installation of accessories such as ambient/mood lighting or another aftermarket modification. It's also worth noting that accessory installers are not always familiar with newly launched models. In the absence of the correct removal procedure or trim tools, excessive force can inadvertently damage interior components like AC vents. Another point to consider is that the VF7 is a CKD model assembled in India and is sold across multiple geographies. Both the Indian and Indonesian assembly plants cater to markets including the Middle East and Africa. Given that the Middle East experiences significantly harsher temperatures than most parts of India, one would expect widespread reports from those markets if this were an inherent thermal or manufacturing defect. Based on the available evidence, I am not convinced this is a manufacturing defect. Of course, I could be proven wrong if there are multiple documented cases of similar failures. It would be worthwhile checking VinFast owner forums across different regions to see whether this is a recurring issue or an isolated incident.

thread_title: Mahindra B07 electric SUV to be launched in 2027
post_content: Mahindra has announced that it will launch its next ‘born-electric’ SUV in 2027. Codenamed B07, the new model will be the production version of the BE.07 concept. Rajesh Jejurikar, Executive Director and CEO (Auto and Farm Sector), Mahindra & Mahindra, said, “We have codenamed B07; it probably won’t be launched with that name. So, B07 will come in some part of calendar 2027. We believe that will be a very big volume driver on top of what we are doing with our current three products. So, that is what we are expecting as a 2027 launch.” The B07 will be Mahindra’s fourth born-electric SUV after the BE 6, XEV 9e, and XEV 9S. It will be based on the brand’s INGLO skateboard platform. The BE.07 concept showcased in 2022 featured a modern design with sharp edges and massively flared wheel arches. It had C-shaped LED DRLs and taillights just like the BE 6. Link to Team-BHP News
